title: Callbacks & Connections
bio:
Workshop Description

A good callback or connection can bring down the house, or help you blow out your game in new, fun ways. We’ll work on callbacks & connections, game, point of view, second beats, all that good stuff to level up your improv.


Instructor Info

Sarah Claspell is an actor/comedian/writer living in Los Angeles. She co-owns and teaches at World’s Greatest Improv School, teaches at the Upright Citizens Brigade, and performs regularly with improv teams The Bozos, Cardinal Redbird, Voltron, Living Room Living Room, and co-hosts the variety show Asian AF. She has performed at SF Sketchfest, Das Improv Festival, The Big Scene in London, Vietnam Improv Festival, Edinburgh Fringe and Edinburgh International Improv Festival. She has been featured on tv shows such as Brooklyn Nine-Nine, Make Some Noise on Dropout, and others. Sarah also co-hosts the podcast Everything is Rent, a podcast about the Broadway musical Rent.

title: Writing and Producing a Short Film
bio:
Workshop Description

So you’ve got an idea for a short film. Or an idea for a feature that you want to shoot as a proof of concept. Or maybe you don’t have any ideas yet, but you’re tired of waiting around for someone else to cast you, staff you as a writer, and/or hire you as a director, and everyone keeps telling you to make your own shit. Or maybe you've made a short and want to learn about cool festivals that offer money for you to screen your film and attend the fest. This 2 hour workshop will cover turning your idea into a reality - how to go from conception to screening at film festivals. We’ll watch a few shorts, discuss short film grants you can apply for as well as film festival and crowdfunding strategies, and workshop your ideas. You’ll walk out with a plan for next steps, a list of film festivals, and be inspired creatively to take your career into your own hands.


Instructor Info

Joy Regullano is a writer / actor / comedian based in LA who wrote on the animated show MONSTERS AT WORK (based on MONSTERS INC) on Disney Plus. Previously, she wrote on JELLY, BEN, and POGO (a PBS Kids web series), KUNG FU PANDA: DRAGON KNIGHT (Netflix / Dreamworks), HEALING POWERS OF DUDE (Netflix), several Sesame Workshop digital shorts, and she was a Sesame Street writing fellow. TV acting credits include BARRY, LINCOLN LAWYER, CRAZY EX-GIRLFRIEND, MODERN FAMILY, SPEECHLESS, and SUPERNATURAL. She has performed improv and sketch around LA at UCB and Second City Hollywood. Her YouTube sketch WHITE FETISH went viral (1M+ views) and was featured in the Huffington Post, Upworthy, and more. She was recently nominated for an Emmy for writing on Sesame Street’s Word of the Day series. She has taught film writing, sketch writing, and pilot writing for Second City Hollywood as well as sketch writing for Improv Hawaii. She has also taught improv, writing, and acting workshops for Pacific Symphony’s summer camp Arts-X-Press, Canyon Kids Film Lab, and the Glendale Adventist girls volleyball team. She won a Birns & Sawyer / Fil Am Creative Film Festival camera grant, and her short films Te Seguiré a la Oscuridad, I Won’t Miss You, and White Fetish have played in dozens of festivals over the years and won multiple awards.

title: Chicago Style Improv
bio:
Workshop Description

Premise-based improv can be super fun, fast-paced, and allow you to heighten and explore with certainty. But how do you improvise with someone unfamiliar with “the game of scene?” In this three-hour workshop, Jonathan Lee-Rey, Executive Artistic Director of Stir Friday Night and an iO faculty member, will teach participants how to turn their emotional authenticity into successful, engaging scene work.


Instructor Info

Jonathan Lee-Rey is an actor, writer, and filmmaker from Yonkers, NY with a splash of the Bronx. Currently, he is based in Chicago where he is the Executive Artistic Director of Stir Friday Night, a teacher at iO theater, a cast member of Escándalo, and the Community Outreach Manager of Stepping Stone Theater. Formerly he was on the iO Harold team Velvet and a member of Generation LatinX. He also made shorts with the iO Network team Free Trial Run and the indie film studio Make it Up Media. He has trained at UCB, iO, Second City, The Magnet and is a graduate of The Harold Ramis Film School and Skidmore College.

title: How Do I Start My Career?
bio:
Workshop Description

How do I audition for SNL? How do I get representation? Can I improvise on a self-tape? There's no road map in going from improv/sketch to the next phase of your career. I wish someone explained what pursuing comedy looks like, both on a granular level (how do I shoot a self-tape?) and on a macro level (do I deserve to do this?). After 10 years of making mistakes, I will compress everything I learned into this one day workshop for you!


Instructor Info

Woody Fu (he/him) is an actor and writer based in Los Angeles. He was a “New Face of Comedy” at the Just For Laughs Festival. You may have seen him on ABC, CBS, FX, Max, HULU, Comedy Central, Peacock, and Netflix, sharing the screen with Will Ferrell, Ryan Reynolds, Awkwafina, Roy Wood Jr, Molly Shannon, Lisa Kudrow, Amy Schumer, and Jack Quaid. You can also see Woody in Vince Gilligan’s new series Pluribus. How did he get here? Originally from New York, Woody is a veteran of the UCB Theater, where he regularly performed improv, musical improv, sketch and characters. These comedy skills took him around the world. From Boom Chicago in Amsterdam, where he created an original sketch revue as the company’s first Asian American actor, to Edinburgh Fringe, where he joined the smash hit institution Baby Wants Candy and the 5-Star parody Thrones! The Musical. His solo show Asian Gracefully was featured in The New York Times, and his characters show Too Many Asians! ran at UCB, and toured Los Angeles and Montreal. The award-winning Woody Fu: One-Man John Wick enjoyed a 5-star sold out run at Edinburgh Fringe. Woody is passionate about creating content that speaks to the Asian American experience, and his digital shorts tackle everything from sexuality, stereotypes, and generational trauma (the fun kind) to toxicity, anime, and inter-Asian racism. They’ve been featured on Vulture, Slamdance, HuffPost and Funny Or Die, and have garnered dozens of laurels at film festivals across the country. He has taught at the Magnet Theater, UCB, BCC, Camp Improv Utopia, and Boom Chicago. woodyfu.com / Insta: @woodyfu

title: Improvised Blockbuster
bio:
Workshop Description

Go full Hollywood and learn the improvised movie format! Lovers will reunite in the rain, loose cannon detectives will walk away from explosions, and wizards will battle kaiju - all in your scenes!


Instructor Info

Donald Chang is a NYC based, Korean actor, VA, comedian and writer. You can see him on HBO, CBS, Netflix and Disney+. You can hear his voice on TV, video games, audio books, and even the Calm app. He regularly improvises on ASSSScat and the weekend team The Prophecy, and performs characters on Cabal.

title: Acting Technique for Sketch & Improv
bio:
Workshop Description

Led by Ryan Chittaphong, Director of Artistic & Student Engagement at the Stella Adler Studio of Acting (and UCB regular), participants will learn the foundation of Stella Adler's teachings and the acting techniques utilized by many artists in the film, television and theater industries. In this hands-on seminar participants explore actions, circumstance and justification; and make courageous, expansive onstage choices using their limitless imaginations as their primary resource.


Instructor Info

Ryan Chittaphong has been with the Stella Adler Studio since 2008 where in addition to serving as Director of Artistic & Student Engagement, he teaches Acting Technique, Character and Improvisation. Ryan also oversees the marketing and recruitment departments of the studio. At the Stella Adler Studio he has been mentored in the technique by Master Teachers Ron Burrus, Antonio Merenda, Betsy Parrish and Artistic Director Tom Oppenheim. He studied improvisation and sketch comedy at the Upright Citizens Brigade and Magnet Theater. Ryan frequently performs improv comedy in New York on house teams at Upright Citizens Brigade, The Armory Comedy, and in the hit monthly Ten Bones Theatre show “Entirely From Memory” at Littlefield. He is currently co-producer of the popular Asian comedy variety show “ASIAN AF” at UCB. He also performs with the Magnet Theater, People’s Improv Theater, Brooklyn Comedy Collective, Second City New York, and other indie groups.

title: Get Out of Your Head And Into Your Feelings!
bio:
Workshop Description

A cure to over-complicated heady improv scenes: Check in with a feeling! This workshop focuses on harnessing emotion to provide hardy engines for your improv scenes. We’ll explore how this approach makes scenes easy, and I share why I think it’s the best!


Instructor Info

Lilan Bowden is an actress and director based out of Los Angeles. She plays “Tia” on Apple TV’s Emmy Award winning show SHRINKING, “Robin Knight” on NCIS, “Amber Kang” on Netflix’s MURDERVILLE, and has had many other notable roles in television shows such as PARKS AND RECREATION, LOVE, THE PETE HOLMES SHOW, along with her breakout role “Bex” in Disney Channel’s first TV show to feature an Asian American family, ANDI MACK (Peabody/BAFTA nominated/Honors Academy Award winner). She is an alum of the Disney Entertainment Television (DET) Directing Program, where she directed the multi-cam comedy VILLIANS OF VALLEY VIEW. Her directorial debut film BECOMING EDDIE was an Official Selection at film festivals across the country and inspired the collaboration with Sony Pictures Entertainment for TV show development. She has performed live comedy at the Los Angeles Upright Citizens Brigade Theater for over 10 years with improv team Rococo and sketch team Bonafide, and with shows she co-produced, Lilan and Wilder’s Best Day Ever (sketch comedy). She continues to perform in various improv shows and, of course, the long running variety comedy show Asian AF.

title: Write A Comedy Song 101
bio:
Workshop Description

Learn how to write a musical comedy song from A to Z. In the class, I will share my tried and true methods for writing a musical comedy song. Together, we will choose a topic, go over outlining and format and write a full musical comedy song together! Musical experience is welcome, but not necessary!


Instructor Info

Shilpa Das is a writer/actor/comedian based in LA. She has been a writer and actor on UCB's long running scripted musical comedy company, Quick & Funny Musicals since 2018. Shilpa has performed musical improv for many years as a member of teams including rap/musical group Kaboombox, UCB mess hall team, Almost Midnight, current running group, Sweet Sweet Fantasy, and as a guest performer with Baby Wants Candy in Shamilton. She's also appeared in various comedy musicals in LA including Bachelor the Musical, Tuckcracker, Heated Rivalry: The Musical Parody! and . She is also known for her work as the producer/co-host of the South Asian AF show series.
